[[54:7|and I will fly|Et volabo]] on the wing of contemplation, gazing on heavenly things, for love of which I despise earthly things and willingly bear adversities; [[54:7|and be at rest|et requiescam]] in God, through faith and charity and inward peace, away from the tumult of earthly things, and the restlessness of the passions and the anxiety of temporal affairs: as was said above, [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest|In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam]].

paras.t: Ecce elongavi me ipsum affectu seu loco, vita et voto, a peccatoribus et inquietis hominibus, fugiens pericula mundi, ne cum perversis pervertar ; et mansi in solitudine, id est, soli Deo vacare tentavi ; vel etiam in loco deserto moram feci, ut Deo liberius adhærerem, atque in eo suavius repausarem. Maxime enim confert solitarius locus ad vitam quietam et speculativam. Propter quod per Osee Dominus ait animæ sibi devotæ : Ecce ego lactabo eam, et ducam eam in solitudinem, et loquar ad cor ejus. Et Jeremias : Quis dabit me in solitudine diversorium viatorum, et derelinquam populum meum ? Unde et Christus Apostolis dixit, sicut Marcus testatur : Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et requiescite pusillum.
paras.en: [[54:8|Lo, I have gone far off|Ecce elongavi]], removing myself in affection or in place, in life and in vow, from sinners and restless men, [[54:8|flying away|fugiens]] from the dangers of the world, lest with the perverse I be perverted[[Ps 17:27||]]; [[54:8|and I abode in the wilderness|et mansi in solitudine]], that is, I have tried to be free for God alone [soli Deo vacare: Denis's gloss on solitudine, "solitude", plays on soli, "alone"]; or else I made my stay in a desert place, that I might cleave to God more freely and rest in him more sweetly. For a solitary place helps very greatly toward a quiet and contemplative life. For which reason the Lord says by Osee to the soul devoted to him: [[Osee 2:14|behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart|Ecce ego lactabo eam, et ducam eam in solitudinem, et loquar ad cor ejus]]. And Jeremias: [[Jer 9:2|Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men, and I will leave my people|Quis dabit me in solitudine diversorium viatorum, et derelinquam populum meum]]? Hence Christ too said to the Apostles, as Mark testifies: [[Mark 6:31|Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little|Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et requiescite pusillum]].

paras.t: Exspectabam eum, id est, longanimiter sustinui, et in ipso speravi, qui salvum me fecit, per gratiam suam, a pusillanimitate spiritus, et tempestate adversitatum et periculorum, quas habui, vel habuissem, nisi gratia Dei me conservasset. Non debemus esse pusillanimes nec præsumptuosi, sed magnanimes, humiles, fortes, semper confidendo in Domino, dicentes cum Apostolo : Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat.
paras.en: [[54:9|I waited for him|Exspectabam eum]], that is, I have patiently endured, and hoped in him, [[54:9|that hath saved me|qui salvum me fecit]] by his grace [[54:9|from pusillanimity of spirit|a pusillanimitate spiritus]] [that is, faintness or smallness of heart, the vice opposed to magnanimity], [[54:9|and a storm|et tempestate]] of adversities and dangers, which I had, or would have had, had not the grace of God preserved me. We ought to be neither faint-hearted nor presumptuous, but great-hearted, humble and strong, ever trusting in the Lord, and saying with the Apostle: [[Phil 4:13|I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me.|Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat]]

paras.t: Consequenter orat Ecclesia seu fidelis pro exstirpatione hæreticorum, schismaticorum, tyrannorum et persecutorum, ac hostium boni communis hominumque justorum. Præcipita, Domine, id est dejice, et divide, id est, ab invicem separa, ne sibi in malo consentiant, linguas eorum, id est sermones et studia prædictorum Ecclesiam perturbantium, seu detractorum et innocentes opprimentium. Non orat Ecclesia ut penitus pereant, sed ut in præsenti corrigantur, et a malo cohibeantur, vel temporaliter affligantur, seu etiam occidantur, si Ecclesia aliter pacem adipisci non potest, vel conservare bonum commune.
paras.en: Next the Church, or the faithful soul, prays for the rooting out of heretics, schismatics, tyrants and persecutors, and of the enemies of the common good and of just men. [[54:10|Cast down, O Lord|Præcipita, Domine]], that is, throw down, [[54:10|and divide|et divide]], that is, separate from one another, lest they agree together in evil, [[54:10|their tongues|linguas eorum]], that is, the speeches and endeavours of those aforesaid who disturb the Church, or of detractors and of those who oppress the innocent. The Church does not pray that they perish utterly, but that in the present life they be corrected and restrained from evil, or afflicted in temporal things, or even put to death, if the Church cannot otherwise obtain peace or preserve the common good.

paras.t: Quoniam vidi iniquitatem et contradictionem, id est perversitatem, perfidiam, schisma et fidei impugnationem, in civitate, id est in militante Ecclesia, in qua semper mali cum bonis miscentur. Oportet enim hæreses esse, et necesse est ut veniant scandala. Die ac nocte, id est semper usque ad finem mundi, circumdabit eam, puta Ecclesiam, super muros ejus, id est in prælatis, pastoribus, atque principibus ejus, iniquitas. Nam superiores aliqui in populo christiano, inferiores inficiunt, opprimunt, scandalizant, aut simili modo pervertunt, sicut Daniel ait : Iniquitas egressa est de Babylone a senioribus, qui videbantur regere populum. Sic, proh dolor ! modo est. Nam qui esse deberent aliorum defensores, muri seu firmamentum, facti sunt animarum corruptores atque maceriæ direptores, quemadmodum per Osee Dominus ait : Attendite, sacerdotes, quoniam laqueus facti estis speculationi, et sicut rete expansum super montem. Et labor in medio ejus et injustitia, id est, in medio Ecclesiæ inveniuntur labor seu violentia, oppressio, inordinatio, culpa pœnalis, et laboriosa iniquitas. Multi enim sunt vocati, et pauci electi. Propterea in medio populi christiani abundant hæc mala, secundum quod per Osee scriptum est : Maledictum, et homicidium, et furtum, et adulterium, et mendacium inundaverunt, et sanguis sanguinem tetigit. Et non defecit de plateis ejus, id est de particularibus Ecclesiis seu sacerdotibus, qui essent aliis iter ad Deum, usura et dolus. Nam et hæc mala in Ecclesiarum rectoribus ac subditis reperiuntur, quoniam omnes (ut ait Jeremias) avaritiæ student, et omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt, non quæ Jesu Christi, secundum Apostolum.
paras.en: [[54:10|for I have seen iniquity and contradiction|Quoniam vidi iniquitatem et contradictionem]], that is, perversity, faithlessness, schism and the assailing of the faith, [[54:10|in the city|in civitate]], that is, in the Church militant, in which the wicked are always mingled with the good. For [[1 Cor 11:19|there must be also heresies|Oportet enim hæreses esse]], and [[Matt 18:7|it must needs be that scandals come|necesse est ut veniant scandala]]. [[54:11|Day and night|Die ac nocte]], that is, always, until the end of the world, there shall [[54:11|surround it|circumdabit eam]], namely the Church, [[54:11|upon its walls|super muros ejus]], that is, in its prelates, pastors and princes, [[54:11|iniquity|iniquitas]]. For some superiors among the Christian people infect, oppress, scandalize or in some like way pervert those beneath them, as Daniel says: [[Dan 13:5|iniquity came out from Babylon|Iniquitas egressa est de Babylone]], from the elders, [[Dan 13:5|that seemed to govern the people|qui videbantur regere populum]]. So, alas, it is now. For those who ought to be the defenders of others, their walls and their bulwark, have become corrupters of souls and breakers-down of the enclosure, as the Lord says by Osee: Attend, [[Osee 5:1|O priests|sacerdotes]], for [[Osee 5:1|you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over|laqueus facti estis speculationi]], and as [[Osee 5:1|a net spread|rete expansum]] upon the mountain [the Douay-Rheims has "upon Thabor"]. [[54:11|and in the midst thereof are labour|Et labor in medio ejus]] [[54:12|And injustice|et injustitia]], that is, in the midst of the Church are found labour, or violence, oppression, disorder, guilt that deserves punishment, and toilsome iniquity. For [[Matt 20:16|many are called but few chosen|Multi enim sunt vocati, et pauci electi]][[Matt 22:14||]]. Therefore these evils abound in the midst of the Christian people, according to what is written by Osee: [[Osee 4:2|Cursing|Maledictum]], [[Osee 4:2|and killing, and theft, and adultery|et homicidium, et furtum, et adulterium]], and lying, [[Osee 4:2|have overflowed, and blood hath touched blood|inundaverunt, et sanguis sanguinem tetigit]]. [[54:12|And usury and deceit|usura et dolus]] [[54:12|have not departed from its streets|Et non defecit de plateis ejus]], that is, from the particular churches, or from the priests, who ought to be a way to God for others. For these evils too are found in the rulers of the churches and in their subjects, since all (as Jeremias says) [[Jer 6:13|are given to covetousness|avaritiæ student]], and [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own not the things that are Jesus Christ's|omnes quæ sua sunt quærunt, non quæ Jesu Christi]], according to the Apostle.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Ecclesia, seu fidelis, quam intolerabiles sint persecutiones, quæ inferuntur ab his qui se dicunt amicos esse, et non sunt. Quoniam si inimicus meus, apertus et evidens, maledixisset mihi, obloquendo, insultando, comminando aut imprecando, sustinuissem utique levius atque libentius : quia sic nil rarum aut inopinatum mihi contigisset. Et si is qui oderat me, non solum clam, sed etiam palam, super me, id est contra me, magna locutus fuisset, id est verba animosa et dura, abscondissem me forsitan ab eo. Secundum quod Christus interdum suos discipulos facere docuit, dicens : Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam. Hoc enim aliquando agendum est, non semper : quia si periclitaretur fides, seu bonum commune, aut subditi salus, fugiendum non esset ab eo qui non fugiendo succurrere posset. Tu vero, homo unanimis, confitendo Christum ore, sicut et ego; dux meus : id est, qui aliorum rector fuisti, et ab Ecclesia constitutus eras dux fratrum tuorum in via Dei; vel me interdum in divino obsequio ædificasti, præcessisti, et perduxisti ; et notus meus, habendo eamdem fidem cum me, seu corporaliter agnitus ; qui mecum dulces capiebas cibos, audiendo prædicationem ac sumendo sacramenta Ecclesiæ, antequam sic apostatares a fide ad hæresim, ab unitate ad schisma, a dilectione ad persecutionem, et a vita laudabili ad mores perversos ; in domo Dei ambulavimus cum consensu, id est, in Ecclesia Christi conversati sumus concorditer, quando adhuc stabas in fide et gratia Dei. De talibus namque ait Joannes : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum.
paras.en: Next the Church, or the faithful soul, shows how unbearable are the persecutions inflicted by those who say they are friends, and are not. [[54:13|For if my enemy|Quoniam si inimicus meus]], open and manifest, [[54:13|had reviled me|maledixisset mihi]], by railing, insulting, threatening or cursing, [[54:13|I would verily have borne with it|sustinuissem utique]] more lightly and more willingly: for so nothing strange or unexpected would have befallen me. [[54:13|And if he that hated me|Et si is qui oderat me]], not only in secret but also openly, [[54:13|against me|super me]], that is, in opposition to me, [[54:13|had spoken great things|magna locutus fuisset]], that is, bold and harsh words, [[54:13|I would perhaps have hidden my self from him|abscondissem me forsitan ab eo]]. So Christ taught his disciples to do at times, saying: [[Matt 10:23|when they shall persecute you|Quum persecuti vos fuerint]] in one city, [[Matt 10:23|flee into another|fugite in aliam]] [the margin gives Matth. v, 23; the passage is Matt 10:23]. For this is to be done sometimes, not always: for if the faith, or the common good, or the salvation of subjects were in danger, he who could bring help by not fleeing ought not to flee from the persecutor. [[54:14|But thou a man of one mind|Tu vero, homo unanimis]], confessing Christ with thy mouth, as I do; [[54:14|my guide|dux meus]]: that is, thou who wast a ruler of others, and hadst been set by the Church as leader of thy brethren in the way of God; or who at times didst edify me in the service of God, go before me and lead me on; [[54:14|and my familiar|et notus meus]], having the same faith as I, or known to me in the body; [[54:15|Who didst take sweetmeats together with me|qui mecum dulces capiebas cibos]], by hearing the preaching and receiving the sacraments of the Church, before thou didst thus fall away from the faith to heresy, from unity to schism, from love to persecution, and from a praiseworthy life to perverse ways; [[54:15|in the house of God we walked with consent|in domo Dei ambulavimus cum consensu]], that is, we lived together in concord in the Church of Christ, when thou didst still stand in the faith and grace of God. For of such John says: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|sed non erant ex nobis ; nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum]].

paras.t: Veniat mors super illos : id est, digni sunt morte spirituali, videlicet ut in præsenti careant vita gratiæ, atque in futuro vita gloriæ. Non enim optando, sed prænuntiando hoc dicitur, vel se divinæ justitiæ conformando. Juxta quem sensum ait Christus seu quilibet justus per Jeremiam : Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me ; ne propitieris iniquitati eorum, et peccatum eorum non deleatur. Et descendant in infernum viventes, id est cum corpore et anima, in die extremi judicii : cujus descensus figura exstitit deglutitio Dathan et Abiron et Core, quos terra vivos absorbuit. Quoniam nequitiæ in habitaculis eorum. In præcedenti explanatione sensus horum patet.
paras.en: [[54:16|Let death come upon them|Veniat mors super illos]]: that is, they are worthy of spiritual death, namely that in the present they should lack the life of grace, and in the future the life of glory. For this is said not by way of wishing, but by way of foretelling, or of conforming oneself to the divine justice. In which sense Christ, or any just man, says by Jeremias: [[Jer 18:23|thou, O Lord, knowest all their counsel against me|Tu, Domine, scis omne consilium eorum adversum me]]; forgive [[Jer 18:23|not their iniquity|ne propitieris iniquitati eorum]], [[Jer 18:23|and let not their sin be blotted out|et peccatum eorum non deleatur]]. [[54:16|and let them go down alive into hell|Et descendant in infernum viventes]], that is, with body and soul, on the day of the last judgment: of which descent the swallowing up of Dathan and Abiron and Core, whom the earth swallowed alive, was a figure[[Num 16:32||]][[Num 16:33||]]. [[54:16|For there is wickedness in their dwellings|Quoniam nequitiæ in habitaculis eorum]]. The sense of these words is plain from the preceding explanation.

paras.t: Ego autem ad Deum clamavi : quia oportet sine intermissione orare, et in omni necessitate atque periculo ad Deum cum omni affectu confugere. Et Dominus salvavit me : non enim derelinquit sperantes in se; sed omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit. Propter quod Dominus ad Jeremiam ait : Eruens liberabo te, et erit tibi anima tua in salutem, quia in me habuisti fiduciam.
paras.en: [[54:17|But I have cried to God|Ego autem ad Deum clamavi]]: for [[Luke 18:1|we ought always to pray|oportet sine intermissione orare]] [Denis has "without ceasing", as in 1 Thess 5:17], and in every need and danger to flee to God with all our affection. [[54:17|and the Lord will save me|Et Dominus salvavit me]] [Denis reads salvavit, "hath saved"]: for he does not forsake those who hope in him; but [[Matt 7:8|every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth|omnis qui petit, accipit; et qui quærit, invenit]]. For which reason the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 39:18|delivering, I will deliver thee|Eruens liberabo te]], and [[Jer 39:18|thy life shall be saved for thee, because thou hast put thy trust in me|erit tibi anima tua in salutem, quia in me habuisti fiduciam]].

paras.t: Vespere et mane et meridie, id est tota die ex his horis constante ; vel, Vespere, id est in statu incipientium, et mane, id est in statu proficientium, et meridie, id est in statu perfectorum ; vel, Vespere et mane et meridie, id est in fine, principio et medio vitæ meæ : narrabo quoad me ipsum, et annuntiabo aliis documenta legis divinæ, et opera Salvatoris, ac alia quæque salutaria : sicut docet Apostolus, Implemini, inquiens, Spiritu Sancto, loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis, et hymnis, et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino, gratias agentes pro omnibus semper. Et exaudiet ipse Dominus vocem meam, qua ipsum laudo et invoco.
paras.en: [[54:18|Evening and morning, and at noon|Vespere et mane et meridie]], that is, the whole day, which is made up of these hours; or, [[54:18|Evening|Vespere]], that is, in the state of beginners, [[54:18|and morning|et mane]], that is, in the state of those making progress, [[54:18|and at noon|et meridie]], that is, in the state of the perfect; or, [[54:18|Evening and morning, and at noon|Vespere et mane et meridie]], that is, at the end, the beginning and the middle of my life: [[54:18|I will speak|narrabo]] as regards myself, [[54:18|and declare|et annuntiabo]] to others the teachings of the divine law, and the works of the Saviour, and all other things that make for salvation: as the Apostle teaches, [[Eph 5:18|be ye filled|Implemini]], he says, [[Eph 5:18|with the Holy Spirit|Spiritu Sancto]], [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis, et hymnis, et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]], [[Eph 5:20|Giving thanks always for all things|gratias agentes pro omnibus semper]]. [[54:18|and he shall hear|Et exaudiet]] (the Lord himself) [[54:18|my voice|vocem meam]], with which I praise him and call upon him.

paras.t: Redimet in pace animam meam ab his qui appropinquant mihi ut noceant, eripiendo me de eorum insidiis, pacemque præstando interioribus meis. Hoc est verbum amorosæ fiduciæ. Quoniam inter multos vocatos, non electos, erant mecum, loco, non mente ; corporaliter, non spiritualiter ; fide, non moribus. Persecutores enim Ecclesiæ et justorum, inter vocatos (qui multi sunt) corpore adsunt electis, sed vita et moribus distant ab eis. Exaudiet Deus preces meas, et humiliabit illos, eo modo quo humiliabuntur in futuro, qui se exaltant in sæculo isto. Non enim est illis commutatio : quoniam converti despiciunt. Unde Apostolus ait : Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita, sciens quia subversus est qui hujusmodi est. De talibus quoque Isaias ait : Dixistis, Percussimus fœdus cum morte, et cum inferno fecimus pactum.
paras.en: [[54:19|He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me|Redimet in pace animam meam ab his qui appropinquant mihi]] to do me harm, by snatching me from their snares, and granting peace to my inmost self. This is a word of loving confidence. [[54:19|for among many|Quoniam inter multos]] called, not chosen, [[54:19|they were with me|erant mecum]], in place, not in mind; in body, not in spirit; in faith, not in morals. For the persecutors of the Church and of the just, among the called (who are many), are present with the elect in body, but are far from them in life and morals. [[54:20|God shall hear|Exaudiet Deus]] my prayers, and [[54:20|shall humble them|humiliabit illos]], in the way in which those who exalt themselves in this world will be humbled in the world to come. [[54:20|For there is no change with them|Non enim est illis commutatio]]: since they scorn to be converted. Hence the Apostle says: [[Tit 3:10|A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid|Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita]], [[Tit 3:11|Knowing that he that is such an one is subverted|sciens quia subversus est qui hujusmodi est]]. Of such too Isaias says: [[Is 28:15|you have said: We have entered into a league with death, and we have made a covenant with hell|Dixistis, Percussimus fœdus cum morte, et cum inferno fecimus pactum]].

paras.t: Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus, id est, legem Christi transgressi sunt, et dicunt se nosse Deum, sed factis negant. Divisi sunt a societate electorum, et separati a caritate et gratia Dei, ab ira vultus ejus, id est justo Dei judicio : et appropinquavit cor illius, id est, Deus, quantum in se est, semper paratus fuit et est misereri, subvenire et parcere.
paras.en: [[54:21|They have defiled his covenant|Contaminaverunt testamentum ejus]], that is, they have transgressed the law of Christ, and [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him|dicunt se nosse Deum, sed factis negant]]. [[54:22|They are divided|Divisi sunt]] from the fellowship of the elect, and separated from the charity and grace of God, [[54:22|by the wrath of his countenance|ab ira vultus ejus]], that is, by the just judgment of God: [[54:22|and his heart hath drawn near|et appropinquavit cor illius]], that is, God, so far as in him lies, always was and is ready to have mercy, to help and to spare.

paras.t: Molliti sunt sermones ejus, scilicet Dei, super oleum : quoniam caritatem et pietatem suam nobis in sacra Scriptura ubertim commendat : quod utique omni melle et oleo dulcius est. Propter quod infra habetur : Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua! super mel ori meo. De quibus eloquiis superius quoque prædictum est : Desideratiora super aurum et lapidem pretiosum multum, et dulciora super mel et favum. Quod Jeremias expertus, ait : Factus sum quasi vir ebrius, et quasi homo madidus vino, a facie Domini, et a facie verborum sanctorum ejus. Quid enim tam mollitum ac dulce, sicut quod ait Paulus apostolus, Propter nimiam caritatem suam, qua dilexit nos Deus Pater, Filium suum misit in similitudinem carnis peccati ? Et Joannes : Sic, inquit, Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret. Et iterum : Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus. Denique dulce est nimis quod per Salomonem æterna Sapientia, Deus altissimus, protestatur : Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum. Et ipsi, videlicet hæretici et hostes Ecclesiæ ac persecutores justorum, sunt jacula : quia veritatem Scripturæ verbis aut factis impugnant, et simplices lædere student. Ideo enim dicit Apostolus : Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit. De quibus apud Job commemoratur : Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini: nescierunt vias Dei, et Deus inultum abire non patitur. Cetera satis exposita sunt.
paras.en: [[54:22|His words are smoother|Molliti sunt sermones ejus]], that is, God's, [[54:22|than oil|super oleum]]: since he commends to us abundantly in Holy Scripture his charity and loving kindness: which is indeed sweeter than any honey or oil. For which reason we have below: [[Ps 118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate! more than honey to my mouth|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua! super mel ori meo]]. And of these words it was also said above: [[Ps 18:11|More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb|Desideratiora super aurum et lapidem pretiosum multum, et dulciora super mel et favum]]. Jeremias, having experienced this, says: [[Jer 23:9|I am become as a drunken man, and as a man full of wine, at the presence of the Lord, and at the presence of his holy words|Factus sum quasi vir ebrius, et quasi homo madidus vino, a facie Domini, et a facie verborum sanctorum ejus]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 9; the passage is Jer 23:9]. For what is so smooth and sweet as what the Apostle Paul says: [[Eph 2:4|for his exceeding charity wherewith he loved us|Propter nimiam caritatem suam, qua dilexit nos]], God the Father sent his Son [[Rom 8:3|in the likeness of sinful flesh|in similitudinem carnis peccati]]? And John says: [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. And again: [[1 John 3:1|Behold what manner of charity the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called and should be the sons of God|Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus]]. Finally, exceedingly sweet is what the eternal Wisdom, God most high, declares by Solomon: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]. [[54:22|and the same|Et ipsi]], namely the heretics and enemies of the Church and persecutors of the just, [[54:22|are darts|sunt jacula]]: because they assail the truth of Scripture by words or deeds, and strive to wound the simple. For this is why the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:17|their speech spreadeth like a canker|Sermo eorum ut cancer serpit]]. Of them it is recorded in Job: [[Job 24:13|They have been rebellious to the light|Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini]]: [[Job 24:13|they have not known his ways|nescierunt vias Dei]], [[Job 24:12|and God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|et Deus inultum abire non patitur]] [the margin gives Job xxiv, 13, 12]. The rest has been sufficiently explained.

paras.t: Ecce ex psalmo isto didicimus quanta Christus sustinuit, et quanta oportet nos ejus exemplo perferre, quum non sit servus major domino suo. Studeamus igitur in sæculo isto omnia dura et aspera pro Christi amore gaudenter portare, pensantes illud Apostoli : Fidelis sermo : nam si commortui sumus, et convivemus ; si sustinemus, et conregnabimus.
paras.en: Behold, from this psalm we have learned how much Christ endured, and how much we must bear after his example, since [[John 13:16|The servant is not greater than his lord|non sit servus major domino suo]]. Let us therefore strive in this world to bear all hard and bitter things gladly for the love of Christ, pondering that saying of the Apostle: [[2 Tim 2:11|A faithful saying: for if we be dead with him, we shall live also with him.|Fidelis sermo : nam si commortui sumus, et convivemus]] [[2 Tim 2:12|If we suffer, we shall also reign with him|si sustinemus, et conregnabimus]].

paras.t: PRECATIO. Omnipotentiam tuam supplices exoramus, qui es ante sæcula, Deus, ut orationem nostram exaudias, ac deprecationem nostram ne despicias : ut qui te salvantem nos expectamus, liberes nos a pusillanimitate spiritus, et omni vitæ et animæ tempestate.
paras.en: Prayer. We humbly entreat thy omnipotence, O God, who art [[54:20|the Eternal|qui es ante sæcula]] [literally "who art before the ages", the words the Douay-Rheims renders "the Eternal"], that thou wouldst [[54:2|hear|exaudias]] our prayer, and [[54:2|despise not|ne despicias]] our supplication: that, as we wait for thee to save us, thou mayest deliver us [[54:9|from pusillanimity of spirit|a pusillanimitate spiritus]], and from every [[54:9|storm|tempestate]] of life and soul.

55.title: EXPLANATIO DE CHRISTO PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI QUINTI : MISERERE MEI, DEUS, QUONIAM CONCULCAVIT, ETC.
55.title_en: Explanation, of Christ, of the fifty-fifth psalm: Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot, etc.

paras.t: Habet autem psalmus jam declarandus hunc titulum : In finem, in carminibus, pro populo qui longe factus est a sanctis, in tituli inscriptione ipsi David, quum tenerent eum allophyli in Geth. Hunc psalmum quidam ad litteram exponunt de David. Communiter autem exponitur de ipsa Ecclesia, seu quolibet fideli multipliciter tribulato. Sed quoniam Christus omnium Prophetarum opus est, debemus (quantum fieri potest) psalmos omnesque Scripturas propheticas de Christo exponere : quia de eo loqui dulcius est, fructuosius, magisque instructivum.
paras.en: Now the psalm next to be explained has this title: [[55:1|Unto the end|In finem]], in songs [*in carminibus*: these words are not in the Douay-Rheims title], [[55:1|for a people that is removed at a distance from the sanctuary|pro populo qui longe factus est a sanctis]], [[55:1|for an inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]], [[55:1|for David|ipsi David]], [[55:1|when the Philistines held him in Geth|quum tenerent eum allophyli in Geth]]. Some expound this psalm literally of David. Commonly, however, it is expounded of the Church herself, or of any of the faithful troubled in many ways. But since Christ is the work [the printed text has *opus*, "work"; the margin suggests *scopus*, "aim"] of all the Prophets, we ought (as far as can be done) to expound the psalms and all the prophetic Scriptures of Christ: because to speak of him is sweeter, more fruitful and more instructive.

paras.t: Sic igitur exponendo hunc psalmum, sensus tituli est : Ipsi David, id est psalmus iste Christo per David significato conveniens, et in finem ultimum, qui est vita æterna, nos dirigens, in carminibus, ita ut Deo in omnibus gratiarum actio referatur, scriptus et editus est pro populo, id est de populo vel contra populum, qui longe factus est, non loco et spatio, sed carendo fide et gratia, a sanctis, id est Christifidelibus, in tituli inscriptione quem posuit Pilatus super caput Christi crucifixi, id est contra Judæos qui titulum istum negaverunt, dicentes Pilato : Noli scribere, Rex Judæorum ; sed quia ipse dixit, Rex sum Judæorum ; quum tenerent eum, scilicet Christum, allophyli, id est gentiles ministri Pilati, quorum quatuor Christum patibulo appenderunt ; in Geth, id est in pressura passionis seu crucis. Per allophylos quoque intelligi possunt ipsi Judæi : quia quemadmodum allophyli seu Palæstini aut Philistæi comprehenderunt David in Geth, perducentes eum ad Achis regem suum ut occideretur ; ita Judæi comprehenderunt Jesum, et vinctum tradiderunt Pontio Pilato ut interficeret eum. Hocque fecerunt in Geth, quod interpretatur pressura, id est in Jerusalem, cui in Evangelio ait Salvator : Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quæ occidis Prophetas ; et denuo, Non capit perire Prophetam extra Jerusalem.
paras.en: Expounding this psalm in this way, then, the sense of the title is: [[55:1|for David|Ipsi David]], that is, this psalm, befitting Christ, who was signified by David, and directing us [[55:1|unto the end|in finem]], the last end, which is eternal life, in songs, so that thanksgiving may be rendered to God in all things, was written and put forth [[55:1|for a people|pro populo]], that is, about the people, or against the people, [[55:1|that is removed at a distance|qui longe factus est]], not in place and space, but by lacking faith and grace, [[55:1|from the sanctuary|a sanctis]], that is, from the faithful of Christ [Denis takes *a sanctis* as "from the saints"; the Douay-Rheims has "from the sanctuary"]; [[55:1|for an inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]], the title which Pilate set over the head of Christ crucified: that is, against the Jews who denied that title, saying to Pilate: [[John 19:21|Write not: The King of the Jews. But that he said: I am the King of the Jews|Noli scribere, Rex Judæorum ; sed quia ipse dixit, Rex sum Judæorum]]; [[55:1|when the Philistines held him|quum tenerent eum]], namely Christ, the Philistines [*allophyli*, "men of another race", the Vulgate's word for the Philistines] being the Gentile servants of Pilate, four of whom hung Christ upon the gibbet; [[55:1|in Geth|in Geth]], that is, in the pressing [*Geth* is interpreted "winepress"; *pressura*, "pressing", also means distress] of the passion or of the cross. By the *allophyli* the Jews themselves may also be understood: for just as the *allophyli*, or Palestinians, or Philistines, seized David in Geth, bringing him to Achis their king that he might be slain[[1 Kings 21:10||]], so the Jews seized Jesus, and bound him and delivered him to Pontius Pilate, that he might put him to death[[Matt 27:1||]][[Matt 27:2||]]. And this they did in Geth, which is interpreted *pressing*, that is, in Jerusalem, to which the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 23:37|Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets|Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quæ occidis Prophetas]]; and again, [[Luke 13:33|it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem|Non capit perire Prophetam extra Jerusalem]].

paras.t: Christus igitur passioni jam appropinquans, secundum quod homo passibilis ait ad Deum Patrem : Miserere mei, Deus, liberando me non a miseriis culpæ, sed pœnæ, id est, de morte et passibili statu transfer me per resurrectionem beatam ad immortalem vitam ac impassibilem statum. Ideo autem oro ut mihi sis misericors, quoniam conculcavit me homo, id est Judas proditor : de quo superius dictum est, Homo pacis meæ, in quo speravi, magnificavit super me supplantationem. Hic, inquam, conculcavit me verbis malignis, et ad conculcandum me vendidit ac prodidit. Tota die, videlicet feria quarta, qua vendidit me, seu quinta, qua tradidit me ipsa nocte, impugnans me occulte, scilicet detrahendo, aliosque ad me impugnandum inducendo, tribulavit me : quia, ut in præcedentis psalmi elucidatione innotuit, tanto fuit persecutio Judæ Christo pœnalior, quanto Judas Christo familiarior exstitit. Quum enim Christus justissimus fuerit, tanto peccatum Judæ ac Judæorum amplius sibi displicuit, quanto illi injustius contra eum fecerunt : et ista displicentia sancta ac justa, tribulatio Christi vocatur. Credendum est quoque, quod Christus, tanquam piissimus, Judæ frequenter condoluit, potissimum passione instante.
paras.en: Christ, then, now drawing near to his passion, says to God the Father, according as he was man and able to suffer: [[55:2|Have mercy on me, O God|Miserere mei, Deus]], by freeing me not from the miseries of guilt but from those of punishment; that is, from death and from the state of suffering bring me over, through a blessed resurrection, to immortal life and a state that cannot suffer. And I pray thee to be merciful to me for this reason, [[55:2|for man hath trodden me under foot|quoniam conculcavit me homo]], that is, Judas the traitor, of whom it was said above: [[Ps 40:10|the man of my peace, in whom I trusted|Homo pacis meæ, in quo speravi]], [[Ps 40:10|hath greatly supplanted me|magnificavit super me supplantationem]]. He, I say, trod me under foot with malicious words, and sold and betrayed me to be trodden under foot. [[55:2|All the day long|Tota die]], namely on the fourth feria [that is, Wednesday], on which he sold me[[Matt 26:14||]], or on the fifth [Thursday], on which he betrayed me that very night[[Matt 26:47||]], [[55:2|fighting against me|impugnans me]] secretly, that is, by slandering me and leading others to fight against me, [[55:2|he hath afflicted me|tribulavit me]]: because, as was made known in the explanation of the preceding psalm[[Ps 54:13||]], the persecution of Judas was the more painful to Christ, the more familiar Judas had been with Christ. For since Christ was most just, the sin of Judas and of the Jews displeased him the more, the more unjustly they acted against him; and this holy and just displeasure is called the tribulation of Christ. It is to be believed also that Christ, being most loving, often grieved for Judas, especially when the passion was at hand.

paras.t: Vel sic : Conculcavit me homo, id est hominum multitudo, videlicet Judæi atque ministri Pilati. Sæpe enim in sacra Scriptura ponitur singulare pro plurali : quemadmodum dixit Judas Simeoni fratri suo, Veni mecum in sortem meam : ubi per Judam et Simeonem intelliguntur tribus seu populi ex Juda et Simeone progeniti. Et in Exodo Dominus ait ad Pharaonem, Dimitte filium meum, ut sacrificet mihi in deserto : ubi per filium intelliguntur filii Israel. Hi ergo conculcaverunt Filium Dei, pro nihilo eum reputantes, opprimentes, et forte etiam corporalibus pedibus eumdem suppeditantes : præsertim in nocte qua viri qui tenebant eum illudebant ei, cædentes conspuentesque eum. Irreverentissime namque eum tractabant, ejusque pœnis se satiabant tota die Parasceves. Impugnans verbis atque verberibus, tribulavit me usque ad mortem homo prædictus, id est homines impii. De quibus apertius subditur :
paras.en: Or thus: [[55:2|man hath trodden me under foot|Conculcavit me homo]], that is, a multitude of men, namely the Jews and the servants of Pilate. For in sacred Scripture the singular is often put for the plural: as Juda said to Simeon his brother, [[Judg 1:3|Come up with me into my lot|Veni mecum in sortem meam]] [Denis has *Veni*, "come", for the Vulgate's *Ascende*, "come up"], where by Juda and Simeon are understood the tribes or peoples descended from Juda and Simeon. And in Exodus the Lord says to Pharao, [[Ex 4:23|Let my son go|Dimitte filium meum]], that he may sacrifice to me in the desert [the Vulgate here has "that he may serve me"; Denis's words are those of the Lord's message about his people, Ex 5:1 and 7:16], where by the son are understood the children of Israel. These, then, trod the Son of God under foot, reckoning him as nothing, oppressing him, and perhaps even trampling him with their bodily feet; above all in the night in which [[Luke 22:63|the men that held him mocked him and struck him|viri qui tenebant eum illudebant ei, cædentes]], spitting upon him as well. For they treated him most irreverently, and [[55:2|all the day long|tota die]] of the Parasceve [that is, the day of Preparation, Good Friday] they sated themselves with his pains[[Job 16:11||]]. [[55:2|Fighting against me|Impugnans]] with words and with blows [*verbis atque verberibus*, a play on words], [[55:2|he hath afflicted me|tribulavit me]] even unto death, the *man* spoken of, that is, wicked men; of whom it is added more plainly:

paras.t: Conculcaverunt me : secundum modum jam dictum ; inimici mei, qui posuerunt adversum me mala pro bonis, et odium pro dilectione mea, tota die præfata ; vel, Tota die, id est toto tempore quo prædicando et miracula perpetrando inter eos conversabar. A principio enim quo Christus prædicare exorsus est, adversabantur ei Judæi, sicut ex evangelica liquet historia. Quoniam multi bellantes adversum me, scilicet principes sacerdotum cum suis fautoribus ; sed ego per patientiam vici eos. Propter quod superius de me legitur : Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio. Hinc quoque Christus apud Jeremiam : Audivi, inquit, contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu persequentium.
paras.en: [[55:3|have trodden on me|Conculcaverunt me]], in the manner just described, [[55:3|My enemies|inimici mei]], who [[Ps 108:5|repaid me evil for good: and hatred for my love|posuerunt adversum me mala pro bonis, et odium pro dilectione mea]], [[55:3|all the day long|tota die]] already spoken of; or, *all the day*, that is, all the time in which I lived among them, preaching and working miracles. For from the beginning, when Christ began to preach, the Jews opposed him, as is clear from the gospel history[[Matt 9:3||]] [the margin lists Matt. ix, 3, 11, 14, 34; xi, 19; xii, 2, 10, 14, 24; xv, 1, 2, 12; xvi, 1; xxi, 15, 16, 23, 46; xxii, 15–17, 23–28, 34–36]. [[55:3|for they are many that make war against me|Quoniam multi bellantes adversum me]], namely the chief priests with their supporters; but I overcame them by patience. Wherefore it is read of me above: [[Ps 23:8|the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle|Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio]]. Hence also Christ in Jeremias: [[Jer 20:10|I heard|Audivi]], he says, [[Jer 20:10|the reproaches of many, and terror on every side|contumelias multorum, et terrorem in circuitu]] of them that persecute me.

paras.t: Ab altitudine diei timebo. Dum aliquis magna tormenta certa die passurus est, dicitur timere illam diem ; et quanto in aliqua hora diei duriora se prænoscit passurum, tanto horam illam amplius formidare asseritur. Passio autem Christi, ab hora noctis qua capiebatur incipiens, et usque ad horam nonam perdurans, continuo augebatur et crevit. Idcirco, eo modo quo Christus passionem sibi instantem naturali affectu abhorruit, etiam diem passionis suæ timebat : et tanto amplius, quo dies illa magis ascendit versus meridiem, quoniam graviora sibi instabant supplicia secundum diei ascensum. Propterea maxime timuit altitudinem diei, in qua præ inæstimabili pœna clamavit : Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Unde et sudor ejus factus est, sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram. Sed timor iste fuit in Christo, tempore trinæ orationis antequam caperetur. Ego vero in te Deo Patre meo sperabo, confidens me conservandum, et resuscitandum, ac glorificandum a te.
paras.en: [[55:4|From the height of the day I shall fear|Ab altitudine diei timebo]]. When someone is to suffer great torments on a certain day, he is said to fear that day; and the harder the things he foresees he will suffer at some hour of the day, the more he is said to dread that hour. Now the passion of Christ, beginning from the hour of the night at which he was taken and lasting until the ninth hour, was continually increased and grew. Therefore, in the way in which Christ by natural affection shrank from the passion at hand, he also feared the day of his passion; and the more so as that day climbed higher towards noon, since heavier torments awaited him as the day rose. Therefore he feared most the height of the day, in which, for pain beyond reckoning, he cried out: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]] Hence too [[Luke 22:44|his sweat became as drops of blood, trickling down upon the ground|sudor ejus factus est, sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram]]. But this fear was in Christ at the time of his threefold prayer, before he was taken. [[55:4|But I will trust in thee|Ego vero in te]], God my Father, confident that I shall be preserved, raised again and glorified by thee.

paras.t: In Deo laudabo sermones meos. Hoc est quod Christus in Evangelio testatur : Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me. Et iterum : Qui a semetipso loquitur, gloriam propriam quærit ; qui autem quærit gloriam ejus qui misit eum, hic verax est. In Deo speravi, ideo non timebo inordinato pavore, quid faciat mihi caro, id est Judæus aut quilibet alius. Quamvis enim Christus ad horam timebat, passione instante, tamen, sicut hunc timorem ex deliberatione rationis assumpsit, sic eum imperio ejusdem cessare fecit. Unde et intrepidus hostibus obviavit, et dixit : Quem quæritis?
paras.en: [[55:5|In God I will praise my words|In Deo laudabo sermones meos]]. This is what Christ testifies in the Gospel: [[John 7:16|My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me|Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus qui misit me]]. And again: [[John 7:18|He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him, he is true|Qui a semetipso loquitur, gloriam propriam quærit ; qui autem quærit gloriam ejus qui misit eum, hic verax est]]. [[55:5|In God I have put my trust|In Deo speravi]], therefore [[55:5|I will not fear|non timebo]] with disordered dread [[55:5|what flesh can do against me|quid faciat mihi caro]], that is, a Jew or anyone else. For although Christ feared for a time, when the passion was at hand, yet, as he took up this fear by the deliberation of reason, so by the command of the same reason he made it cease. Hence he went fearless to meet his enemies, and said: [[John 18:4|Whom seek ye?|Quem quæritis?]][[John 18:7||]]

paras.t: Tota die passionis meæ, vel totis diebus prædicationis meæ, verba mea execrabantur, id est, a Judæis contemnebantur, et male interpretabantur. Dixerunt enim, ut legitur apud Matthæum, Blasphemavit ; et, Reus est mortis ; atque apud Joannem, Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit. Hoc est quod per Amos de Judæis inducitur : Odio habuerunt corripientem, et loquentem perfecte abominati sunt. Ideo namque et Christus dicit : Me odit mundus, quia ego testimonium perhibeo de illo quoniam opera ejus mala sunt. Adversum me omnes cogitationes eorum in malum, videlicet ut me false accusent, atque injuste occidant.
paras.en: [[55:6|All the day long|Tota die]] of my passion, or all the days of my preaching, [[55:6|they detested my words|verba mea execrabantur]], that is, my words were despised by the Jews and wrongly interpreted. For they said, as is read in Matthew, [[Matt 26:65|He hath blasphemed|Blasphemavit]]; and, [[Matt 26:66|He is guilty of death|Reus est mortis]]; and in John, [[John 9:16|This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath|Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit]]. This is what is said of the Jews through Amos: [[Amos 5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh|Odio habuerunt corripientem]], [[Amos 5:10|and have abhorred him that speaketh perfectly|et loquentem perfecte abominati sunt]]. For this reason Christ too says of the world: [[John 7:7|me it hateth, because I give testimony of it, that the works thereof are evil|Me odit mundus, quia ego testimonium perhibeo de illo quoniam opera ejus mala sunt]]. [[55:6|all their thoughts were against me unto evil|Adversum me omnes cogitationes eorum in malum]], namely, that they might falsely accuse me and unjustly slay me.

paras.t: Inhabitabunt : id est, inhabitaverunt infideles Judæi mecum et cum discipulis meis in Synagoga, seu domo Domini, quantum ad fidem, quia dicebant se Deum colere, et Christum regem exspectare : sicque per fidem informem cum credentibus in Deum habitaverunt in Synagoga ; et abscondent, id est, occulte mihi insidiati sunt, tentantes me verbis dolosis. Ipsi calcaneum meum observabunt, id est, opera mea explorabant, quatenus occasionem contra me reperirent. Propter quod scriptum est : Observabant Judæi si sabbatis curaret, ut accusarent eum.
paras.en: [[55:7|They will dwell|Inhabitabunt]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews dwelt with me and with my disciples in the Synagogue, or house of the Lord, as regards faith, because they said that they worshipped God and awaited Christ the king; and so, by an unformed faith [*fides informis*, that is, faith without charity], they dwelt in the Synagogue with those who believed in God; [[55:7|and hide themselves|et abscondent]], that is, they lay in wait for me secretly, tempting me with deceitful words; [[55:7|they will watch my heel|Ipsi calcaneum meum observabunt]], that is, they spied out my works, so as to find occasion against me. Wherefore it is written of the Jews: [[Mark 3:2|they watched him whether he would heal on the sabbath days, that they might accuse him|Observabant Judæi si sabbatis curaret, ut accusarent eum]].

paras.t: Sicut sustinuerunt animam meam pro nihilo, id est, sicut me vilipendebant, et vitam meam exspectabant, quatenus eam pro nihilo, id est, ac si nihil nulliusque reputationis exsisteret, perderent, non arbitrantes esse peccatum occidere me ; salvos facies illos : quasi dicat, Non. Ac si dicat : Quam veraciter bene fecerunt, me taliter persequentes, tam vere eos salvabis. Ideo addit : In ira populos confringes : id est, per vindictam divinæ justitiæ, incredulos meque persequentes Judæos impœnitentes totaliter destrues, quantum ad esse gratiæ et gloriæ, non dando eis aliquod meritorium esse, et etiam in hac vita eos comminuendo, dispergendo, ac humiliando. Hinc enim de eis apud Osee dicitur : Radix eorum exsiccata est ; fructum nequaquam facient. Et per Isaiam Christus de eis locutus est : Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea.
paras.en: [[55:7|As they have waited for my soul|Sicut sustinuerunt animam meam]] [[55:8|For nothing|pro nihilo]] [Denis joins *pro nihilo*, "for nothing", to the words before it: as they waited for my soul as for a thing of nothing], that is, as they held me cheap and waited for my life, that they might destroy it as nothing, that is, as though it were nothing and of no account, not thinking it a sin to kill me; [[55:8|shalt thou save them|salvos facies illos]]: as if to say, No. As if he said: as truly as they did well in persecuting me thus, so truly wilt thou save them. Therefore he adds: [[55:8|in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces|In ira populos confringes]]: that is, through the vengeance of divine justice thou wilt utterly destroy the unbelieving and impenitent Jews who persecute me, as regards the being of grace and of glory, not giving them any meritorious being, and also crushing, scattering and humbling them in this life. For hence it is said of them in Osee: [[Osee 9:16|their root is dried up, they shall yield no fruit|Radix eorum exsiccata est ; fructum nequaquam facient]]. And through Isaias Christ has spoken of them: [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]][[Is 63:6||]].

paras.t: Deus, vitam meam annuntiavi tibi : id est, ad honorem et gloriam nominis tui professus sum aliis conversationis meæ sanctitatem, et omnia quæ feci, coram te feci, et tibi adscripsi. Hoc modo Christus vitam suam Deo Patri annuntiavit, dum asseruit : Diligo Patrem, et sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio ; et alibi, Ego quæ placita sunt ei (scilicet Patri meo) facio semper. Et in Luca quoque, allegans impletum in se quod prædictum fuit per Isaiam : Spiritus, ait, Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me ; ad annuntiandum mansuetis misit me, ut mederer contritos corde. Posuisti lacrimas meas in conspectu tuo, id est, acceptas eas habuisti, idque pro quo lacrimas fudi, implesti. Unde ait Apostolus : Cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces offerens, exauditus est pro sua reverentia. In resuscitatione insuper Lazari lacrimatus est Jesus, et ait : Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me.
paras.en: [[55:8|O God|Deus]], [[55:9|I have declared to thee my life|vitam meam annuntiavi tibi]]: that is, to the honour and glory of thy name I have professed before others the holiness of my conversation, and all that I did, I did before thee and ascribed to thee. In this way Christ declared his life to God the Father, when he asserted: [[John 14:31|I love the Father: and as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Diligo Patrem, et sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]; and elsewhere, [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei (scilicet Patri meo) facio semper]] (him, that is, my Father). And in Luke also[[Luke 4:18||]], alleging that what had been foretold through Isaias was fulfilled in him[[Luke 4:21||]]: [[Is 61:1|The spirit|Spiritus]], he says, [[Is 61:1|of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me|Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me]]: [[Is 61:1|he hath sent me to preach to the meek, to heal the contrite of heart|ad annuntiandum mansuetis misit me, ut mederer contritos corde]] [Denis gives the words of Isaias, not those of Luke 4:18]. [[55:9|thou hast set me tears in thy sight|Posuisti lacrimas meas in conspectu tuo]], that is, thou hast held them acceptable, and hast fulfilled that for which I shed tears. Whence the Apostle says: [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears, offering up prayers|Cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces offerens]], [[Heb 5:7|was heard for his reverence|exauditus est pro sua reverentia]]. Moreover, at the raising of Lazarus [[John 11:35|Jesus wept|lacrimatus est Jesus]], and said: [[John 11:41|Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me|Gratias ago tibi, Pater, quoniam audisti me]].

paras.t: Sicut et in promissione tua, id est, sicut per Prophetas dixisti. Hoc enim prædictum est, quod lacrimas meas ac preces acceptas habere, dicente te de me per beatum Isaiam prophetam : Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum ; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea. Tunc, id est, quum me exaudieris suscitando me a mortuis, convertentur inimici mei, puta Judæi, retrorsum, recedendo a te, et non credendo in me, sicut apud Jeremiam prophetam de eis testatus es : Verterunt ad me tergum, et non faciem. De quibus alibi legitur : Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus ; et non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est, id est Judæi qui dixerunt, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem.
paras.en: [[55:9|As also in thy promise|Sicut et in promissione tua]], that is, as thou hast said through the Prophets. For this was foretold, that thou wouldst hold my tears and prayers acceptable, when thou didst say of me through the blessed prophet Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum ; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]]. [[55:10|Then|Tunc]], that is, when thou hast heard me by raising me from the dead, [[55:10|shall my enemies be turned|convertentur inimici mei]], the Jews, to wit, [[55:10|back|retrorsum]], by withdrawing from thee and not believing in me, as thou didst testify of them in the prophet Jeremias: [[Jer 2:27|they have turned their back to me, and not their face|Verterunt ad me tergum, et non faciem]]. Of whom it is read elsewhere: [[Dan 9:26|after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain: and the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus ; et non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est]], that is, the Jews, who said: [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]].

paras.t: In quacumque die invocavero te, orando pro me ipso aut corpore mystico, scilicet per experientiam, seu experimentalem exauditionem, quoniam Deus meus es specialissimo modo, ubique et semper regens atque exaudiens me.
paras.en: [[55:10|In what day soever I shall call upon thee|In quacumque die invocavero te]], praying for myself or for my mystical body, namely, by experience, or by the experience of being heard [the lemma *ecce cognovi*, "behold I know", which these words explain, is not printed here], [[55:10|thou art my God|quoniam Deus meus es]] in a most special way, everywhere and always ruling me and hearing me.

paras.t: In Deo laudabo verbum, in Domino laudabo sermonem. Unum exponit aliud : id est, quidquid dico aut prædico, ad Deum finaliter referam, ejusque illuminationi adscribam, nec propriam gloriam quæram. Propterea Christus dixit : Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio ; et alias, Ego non quæro gloriam meam. In Deo speravi, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo mihi injuste repugnans.
paras.en: [[55:11|In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech|In Deo laudabo verbum, in Domino laudabo sermonem]]. The one explains the other: that is, whatever I say or preach I will refer in the end to God and ascribe to his enlightening, and I will not seek my own glory. Therefore Christ said: [[John 5:41|I receive not glory from men|Claritatem ab hominibus non accipio]]; and elsewhere, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]] [the margin reads viii, 30; the words are at John 8:50]. [[55:11|In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me|In Deo speravi, non timebo quid faciat mihi homo]], when he opposes me unjustly.

paras.t: In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, id est, in corde meo sunt sancta desideria mihi a te infusa, per quæ tuum honorem hominumque salutem desidero ; quæ reddam laudationes tibi, id est, quæ offeram tibi tanquam sacrificium laudis ac laudandi materiam. Per sancta enim desideria Deus laudatur et honoratur.
paras.en: [[55:12|In me, O God, are vows to thee|In me sunt, Deus, vota tua]] [*vota tua*, literally "thy vows"], that is, in my heart are holy desires poured into me by thee, through which I desire thy honour and the salvation of men; [[55:12|which I will pay, praises to thee|quæ reddam laudationes tibi]], that is, which I will offer thee as a sacrifice of praise and as matter for praising. For by holy desires God is praised and honoured.

paras.t: Quoniam eripuisti animam meam de morte in die resurrectionis, uniendo eam corpori, a quo per mortem exstitit separata ; et pedes meos de lapsu : id est, omnes operationes meas gratia præveniente præservasti a ruina peccati, ita ut nunquam cecidi, sed tibi placentia incessabiliter egi. Et hoc ideo tu fecisti, ego quoque idcirco hæc ad gloriam tuam profiteor, ut placeam coram Deo in lumine viventium, id est, ut tibi complaceam, et in te, et non in me, complacentiam habeam : placeam, inquam, coram te, in lumine viventium, id est in splendidissima patria Beatorum, ubi coram Deo adsisto interpellans pro mundo : quemadmodum ad Hebræos inducit Apostolus, Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit, sed in ipsum cœlum, ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis.
paras.en: [[55:13|Because thou hast delivered my soul from death|Quoniam eripuisti animam meam de morte]] on the day of the resurrection, by uniting it to the body from which it had been separated by death; [[55:13|my feet from falling|et pedes meos de lapsu]]: that is, by prevenient grace [grace that goes before and moves the will] thou hast preserved all my works from the ruin of sin, so that I never fell, but did unceasingly the things that please thee. And thou hast done this, and I too profess these things to thy glory, for this end: [[55:13|that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living|ut placeam coram Deo in lumine viventium]], that is, that I may be well-pleasing to thee, and take my pleasure in thee and not in myself: may please, I say, in thy sight, in the light of the living, that is, in the most splendid fatherland of the Blessed, where I stand before God interceding for the world; as the Apostle brings in to the Hebrews: [[Heb 9:24|Jesus is not entered into the Holies made with hands|Non in manufacta sancta Jesus introiit]], [[Heb 9:24|but into Heaven itself, that he may appear now in the presence of God for us|sed in ipsum cœlum, ut appareat nunc vultui Dei pro nobis]].

paras.t: Christus igitur sibi in se non placuit, sed in Deo, id est in se ipso, secundum quod Deus fuit, vel in Deo Patre ac sancta Trinitate. Et quomodo ergo nos miseri, tam vanissimi atque stultissimi unquam efficimur, ut placeamus nobismetipsis, alios contemnendo, atque in nobis gloriando ? Advertamus admonitionem S. Pauli : Debemus, inquit, nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere, et non nobis placere. Etenim Christus non sibi placuit.
paras.en: Christ, then, did not please himself in himself, but in God: that is, in himself according as he was God, or in God the Father and the holy Trinity. How then do we wretches, so utterly vain and foolish, ever come to please ourselves, despising others and glorying in ourselves? Let us heed the admonition of St Paul, who says: [[Rom 15:1|we that are stronger ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves|nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere, et non nobis placere]]. [[Rom 15:3|For Christ did not please himself|Etenim Christus non sibi placuit]].

55.title: ELUCIDATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM PSALMI QUINQUAGESIMI QUINTI
55.title_en: Moral explanation of the same fifty-fifth psalm.

paras.t: TROPOLOGICE denique exponendo hunc psalmum, præinductus titulus sic intelligendus est: In finem, id est psalmus iste in Christum nos dirigens, scriptus pro populo qui longe factus est a sanctis, id est, qui vita et moribus discordat ab electis, in tituli inscriptione: quia titulum crucifixi, videlicet, Hic est rex Judæorum, quem sancti fide et opere venerantur, ipsi vel vita reproba, vel mente incredula negant. Psalmus, inquam, ipsi David, id est conveniens Ecclesiæ, seu fideli per David figurato, quum tenerent eum allophyli in Geth, id est, quum undique vallarent alienigenæ a caritate et fide formata ipsam Ecclesiam seu quemlibet Christianum, tribulationibus, tentationibus atque pressuris.
paras.en: Finally, expounding this psalm tropologically [that is, according to the moral sense], the title set before it is to be understood thus: [[55:1|Unto the end|In finem]], that is, this psalm directing us to Christ, written [[55:1|for a people that is removed at a distance from the sanctuary|pro populo qui longe factus est a sanctis]] [the Latin *a sanctis* can mean "from the holy things" or "from the saints"; Denis takes it in the second sense], that is, for those who in life and conduct are at variance with the elect, [[55:1|for an inscription of a title|in tituli inscriptione]]: because the title of the Crucified, namely, [[Luke 23:38|THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS|Hic est rex Judæorum]], whom the saints venerate by faith and works, these deny either by a reprobate life or by an unbelieving mind. A psalm, I say, [[55:1|for David|ipsi David]], that is, suited to the Church, or to the faithful soul figured by David, [[55:1|when the Philistines held him in Geth|quum tenerent eum allophyli in Geth]] [*allophyli*, literally "men of another race"; hence Denis's "aliens"], that is, when those who are aliens to charity and to formed faith [that is, faith given its form and life by charity] beset the Church herself, or any Christian, on every side with tribulations, temptations and pressures.

paras.t: Ecclesia ergo, quæ modo adversitatibus velut in torculari comprimitur, quilibetque fidelis persecutionibus multis circumdatus, clamet ad Deum: Miserere mei, Deus, id est, tu, creator, gubernator, salvator, judexque meus, qui naturaliter pius es, et totus misericors, mihi misero condole, non pœnalem affectum habendo, sed clementer atque celeriter succurrendo. Vehementer namque indigeo, quoniam conculcavit me homo detractor, læsor, animarum corruptor, caritatis persecutor, innocentiæ adversator, pede elationis contumeliose me opprimens. De quo pede superius dictum est: Non veniat mihi pes superbiæ.
paras.en: The Church, therefore, which is now pressed by adversities as in a winepress, and every faithful soul surrounded by many persecutions, should cry to God: [[55:2|Have mercy on me, O God|Miserere mei, Deus]], that is: thou, my Creator, Ruler, Saviour and Judge, who art by nature loving and wholly merciful, have compassion on me, a wretch, not by having a feeling of pain [that is, not by suffering with me, which cannot be in God, but by the effect of mercy], but by coming to my help mercifully and quickly. For I am in great need, [[55:2|for man hath trodden me under foot|quoniam conculcavit me homo]]: the detractor, the wounder, the corrupter of souls, the persecutor of charity, the adversary of innocence, insultingly crushing me with the foot of pride. Of which foot it was said above: [[Ps 35:12|Let not the foot of pride come to me|Non veniat mihi pes superbiæ]].

paras.t: Conculcaverunt me inimici mei domestici et extranei, visibiles et invisibiles, occulti et manifesti, tota die naturali, id est tempore diurno atque nocturno, tentando, aspernando, aut simili modo adversando. Quoniam multi sunt bellantes adversum me, qui me a te conantur avertere, et ad vitia inclinare. Pugnant enim contra nos mundus, id est homines sæculares, ut pervertamur cum perversis; caro, id est passiones seu motus sensualitatis, quatenus hominem a medio rectæ rationis abducant; et dæmones. De quibus ait Apostolus: Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principatus et potestates, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus. Quod intelligendum non est, quasi non sit nobis aliqua colluctatio contra carnem et sanguinem, quum dicat Apostolus, Si secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini; et rursus, Quicumque sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Sed hoc ideo dictum est, quia non est nobis colluctatio contra carnem et sanguinem tantum aut principaliter.
paras.en: [[55:3|My enemies have trodden on me|Conculcaverunt me inimici mei]], those of my own household and strangers, visible and invisible, hidden and open, [[55:3|all the day long|tota die]] of the natural day [that is, the whole day of twenty-four hours], that is, by day and by night, tempting, despising, or opposing me in some like way. [[55:3|for they are many that make war against me|Quoniam multi sunt bellantes adversum me]], who strive to turn me away from thee and to bend me toward vices. For there fight against us the world, that is, worldly men, that we may be perverted with the perverse; the flesh, that is, the passions or motions of the sensuality, so as to draw a man away from the mean of right reason; and the demons. Of whom the Apostle says: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principatus et potestates]], [[Eph 6:12|against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]]. This is not to be understood as though we had no wrestling at all against flesh and blood, since the Apostle says, [[Rom 8:13|if you live according to the flesh, you shall die|Si secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini]]; and again, [[Gal 5:24|they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Quicumque sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. But it is said because our wrestling is not against flesh and blood only, or chiefly.

paras.t: Ab altitudine diei timebo, id est, ab ascensu seu processu temporis mihi concessi, formidabo propter pericula mihi instantia. Quo enim diutius vivo, eo frequentius pecco, præsertim quum justus septies cadat in die: idcirco tempus futurum timeo, quia dies mali sunt, eo quod sæpius peccet homo in eis. Vel sic: Ab altitudine diei cujuslibet artificialis, quo victurus sum, timebo: quoniam plures peccandi occasiones occurrunt in die, quam in nocte, præsertim die in altum ascendente. De mane enim est homo ad devotionem habilior, sed circa meridiem obviant corporis gravissimæ necessitudines, quia cibo potuque egemus: quibus acceptis, est homo ad devotionem ineptior. Propterea hanc horam timent devoti, videlicet ne graventur corda eorum crapula, aut ebrietate: ideoque accedunt ad mensam velut ad carcerem.
paras.en: [[55:4|From the height of the day I shall fear|Ab altitudine diei timebo]], that is, from the rising or onward course of the time granted me I shall be afraid, because of the dangers that press upon me. For the longer I live, the more often I sin, especially since [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|justus septies cadat]] in the day: therefore I fear the time to come, [[Eph 5:16|because the days are evil|quia dies mali sunt]], in that man sins more often in them. Or thus: From the height of each artificial day [that is, the day from sunrise to sunset, as against the natural day of twenty-four hours] that I am to live, I shall fear: for more occasions of sinning meet us in the day than in the night, especially as the day climbs on high. For in the morning a man is better disposed for devotion, but toward noon the most pressing needs of the body come in the way, because we need food and drink; and when these have been taken, a man is less fit for devotion. Therefore the devout fear this hour, namely lest their hearts [[Luke 21:34|be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|graventur corda eorum crapula, aut ebrietate]]; and so they go to table as to a prison.

paras.t: Ego vero in te sperabo: id est, quamvis tot malis circumdatus sim, non tamen despero; sed in te incessanter confido quod non succumbam aut vincar, sed in nomine tuo prævaleam, verissime scriptum sciens, Major est qui in vobis est, quam qui in mundo; et dicente beatissimo Eliseo: Noli timere; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis. Cum illis namque est brachium carneum, nobiscum autem est Dominus Deus noster. Unde et per Osee dicitur: Misericordiam et judicium custodi, et spera in Deo tuo semper.
paras.en: [[55:4|But I will trust in thee|Ego vero in te sperabo]]: that is, though I am beset by so many evils, yet I do not despair, but trust in thee unceasingly that I shall not give way or be overcome, but shall prevail in thy name, knowing that it is most truly written, [[1 John 4:4|greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world|Major est qui in vobis est, quam qui in mundo]]; and as the most blessed Eliseus says: [[4 Kings 6:16|Fear not: for there are more with us than with them|Noli timere; plures enim nobiscum sunt, quam cum illis]]. [[2 Par 32:8|For with him is an arm of flesh: with us the Lord our God|Cum illis namque est brachium carneum, nobiscum autem est Dominus Deus noster]] [Denis has "with them", where the Douay-Rheims, following the Vulgate, has "with him"]. Hence it is said by Osee too: [[Osee 12:6|keep mercy and judgment, and hope in thy God always|Misericordiam et judicium custodi, et spera in Deo tuo semper]].

paras.t: In Deo laudabo sermones meos, ad ejus honorem eos ordinando, nec in vana philosophia, sterili eloquentia, sermone rhetorico, verbo præsumptuoso, malo et garrulo, gloriabor; sed in verbo confessionis, orationis, divinæque laudis lætabor. In Deo speravi, non timebo de cetero, timore deiciente et inordinato, quid faciat mihi caro, id est homo carnalis. Non enim timebo eos qui corpus occidunt: quin imo tribulationem tanquam donum Dei recipiam, amplexabor, et hilariter feram, recolens illud Apostoli: Vobis datum est pro Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, verum etiam ut patiamini pro illo.
paras.en: [[55:5|In God I will praise my words|In Deo laudabo sermones meos]], ordering them to his honour; and I shall not glory in vain philosophy[[Col 2:8||]], barren eloquence, rhetorical speech, or presumptuous, evil and babbling talk, but shall rejoice in the word of confession, of prayer and of divine praise. [[55:5|In God I have put my trust|In Deo speravi]]: [[55:5|I will not fear|non timebo]] henceforth, with a fear that casts down and is disordered, [[55:5|what flesh can do against me|quid faciat mihi caro]], that is, carnal man. For I will not fear [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]]: nay rather, I shall receive tribulation as a gift of God, embrace it and bear it cheerfully, recalling that saying of the Apostle: [[Phil 1:29|unto you it is given for Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him|Vobis datum est pro Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, verum etiam ut patiamini pro illo]].

paras.t: Tota die verba mea exsecrabantur. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Maledicimur, et benedicimus. Propter quod etiam Christus ait discipulis suis: Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur. Contemnunt enim atque vituperant impii verba justorum; et sicut Job dicit, Deridetur justi simplicitas. Adversum me omnes cogitationes eorum, videlicet hæreticorum, schismaticorum et perversorum, sunt in malum, ut mihi contrarientur ac noceant, malaque pœnæ et culpæ infligant.
paras.en: [[55:6|All the day long they detested my words|Tota die verba mea exsecrabantur]]. This is what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:12|We are reviled: and we bless|Maledicimur, et benedicimus]]. For which reason Christ too says to his disciples: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]]. For the wicked despise and revile the words of the just; and, as Job says, [[Job 12:4|the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn|Deridetur justi simplicitas]]. [[55:6|All their thoughts were against me|Adversum me omnes cogitationes eorum]], that is, the thoughts of heretics, schismatics and the perverse, are [[55:6|unto evil|in malum]], so as to oppose and harm me, and to inflict on me the evils of punishment and of guilt.

paras.t: Inhabitabunt mecum in Ecclesia militanti, in qua boni et mali miscentur, vel in terra ac sæculo isto, prædicti adversarii mei; et abscondent, id est, fraudulenter et clam nocere nituntur. De talibus siquidem Christus præmonuit: Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces; et iterum, Inimici hominis domestici ejus. Ipsi calcaneum meum observabunt, id est, opera mea explorabunt, non ut imitentur, sed ut criminentur: quemadmodum ad Galatas ait Apostolus, Subintroducti falsi fratres, qui introierunt explorare libertatem nostram, quam habemus in Christo Jesu. Unde superius quoque præhabitum est: Observabit peccator justum, et stridebit super eum dentibus suis.
paras.en: [[55:7|They will dwell|Inhabitabunt]] with me, these adversaries of mine spoken of above, in the Church militant, in which good and bad are mixed, or in this land and this world; [[55:7|and hide themselves|et abscondent]], that is, they strive to do harm by fraud and in secret. Of such indeed Christ warned beforehand: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]]; and again, [[Mich 7:6|a man's enemies are they of his own household|Inimici hominis domestici ejus]] [the margin gives Mich. vii, 6; Denis gives the words as Christ's, who repeats them at Matt 10:36]. [[55:7|they will watch my heel|Ipsi calcaneum meum observabunt]], that is, they will spy out my works, not to imitate them but to accuse them: as the Apostle says to the Galatians, [[Gal 2:4|false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privately to spy our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus|Subintroducti falsi fratres, qui introierunt explorare libertatem nostram, quam habemus in Christo Jesu]]. Hence too it was set down above: [[Ps 36:12|The sinner shall watch the just man: and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.|Observabit peccator justum, et stridebit super eum dentibus suis.]]

paras.t: Sicut sustinuerunt impii animam meam pro nihilo, eam spernendo, scandalizando, aut persequendo, salvos facies illos: id est, non salvabis eos, propter peccata commissa in me; imo, nisi pœnitentiam egerint, æternaliter eos damnabis, sicut merentur. Aliqui autem exponunt istud in bono, ut sit sensus: Sicut sustinuerunt animam meam ad perdendum eam, pro nihilo, id est gratis et sine eorum merito, salvos facies eos. In ira populos confringes, ulciscendo eorum malitiam, eosque damnando. Vel, In ira tuæ paternæ disciplinæ, populos peccatores confringes, deprimendo eorum superbiam, et vitia exstirpando: quemadmodum in Isaia legitur, Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum.
paras.en: [[55:7|As they have waited|Sicut sustinuerunt]], the wicked, that is, [[55:7|for my soul|animam meam]] [[55:8|For nothing|pro nihilo]] [Denis takes *sustinuerunt … pro nihilo* as "they have held my soul for nothing", that is, as worthless], by spurning it, causing it to stumble, or persecuting it, [[55:8|shalt thou save them|salvos facies illos]] [read as a question]: that is, thou wilt not save them, because of the sins committed against me; nay rather, unless they do penance[[Luke 13:5||]], thou wilt damn them eternally, as they deserve. But some expound this in a good sense, so that the meaning is: As they have waited for my soul to destroy it, for nothing, that is, freely and without any merit of theirs, thou shalt save them. [[55:8|in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces|In ira populos confringes]], avenging their malice and damning them. Or: In the anger of thy fatherly discipline thou shalt break the sinful peoples in pieces, by bringing down their pride and rooting out their vices: as is read in Isaias, [[Is 2:17|the loftiness of men shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be humbled|Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum]].

paras.t: Deus, vitam meam annuntiavi tibi, seu tuo vicario, scilicet sacerdoti, humiliter confitendo mea peccata, et tibi attribuendo opera bona. Scriptum est enim: Omnis qui male agit, odit lucem, et non venit ad lucem, ut non arguantur opera ejus; qui autem facit veritatem, venit ad lucem, ut manifestentur opera ejus, quia in Deo sunt facta. Ideo quoque superius dictum est: Revela Domino viam tuam. Posuisti lacrimas meas, quas pro peccatorum indulgentia, seu gloriæ dilatione, aut simili pia causa effudi, in conspectu tuo, habendo eas acceptas, atque pro eis mihi reservans præmium in futuro. Hinc Dominus ad Ezechiam: Audivi (inquit) orationem tuam, vidi lacrimas tuas. Et Jeremias orat: Ne avertas aurem tuam a singultu meo. Sicut et in promissione tua: promisit enim Deus se exauditurum suspiria, desideria, orationes et lacrimas suorum fidelium.
paras.en: [[55:8|O God|Deus]], [[55:9|I have declared to thee my life|vitam meam annuntiavi tibi]], or to thy vicar, namely the priest, by humbly confessing my sins, and by ascribing good works to thee. For it is written: [[John 3:20|every one that doth evil hateth the light and cometh not to the light, that his works may not be reproved|Omnis qui male agit, odit lucem, et non venit ad lucem, ut non arguantur opera ejus]]; [[John 3:21|But he that doth truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest: because they are done in God|qui autem facit veritatem, venit ad lucem, ut manifestentur opera ejus, quia in Deo sunt facta]]. Therefore it was also said above: [[Ps 36:5|Commit thy way to the Lord|Revela Domino viam tuam]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxv, 3; the words are at Ps 36:5]. [[55:9|Thou hast set me tears|Posuisti lacrimas meas]], which I have shed for the pardon of sins, or because glory is delayed, or for some like holy cause, [[55:9|in thy sight|in conspectu tuo]], holding them acceptable, and keeping for me a reward for them in the time to come. Hence the Lord says to Ezechias: [[4 Kings 20:5|I have heard|Audivi]] (he says) [[4 Kings 20:5|thy prayer, and I have seen thy tears|orationem tuam, vidi lacrimas tuas]] [the margin gives IV Reg. v, 5; the words are at 4 Kings 20:5]. And Jeremias prays: [[Lam 3:56|turn not away thy ear from my sighs|Ne avertas aurem tuam a singultu meo]]. [[55:9|As also in thy promise|Sicut et in promissione tua]]: for God has promised that he will hear the sighs, desires, prayers and tears of his faithful.

paras.t: Tunc convertentur inimici mei retrorsum: id est, quum me supplicantem audieris, inimici mei visibiles invisibilesque deficient. Unde et B. Jacobus: Resistite (ait) diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. In quacumque die invocavero te invocatione interna, affectuosa, et stabili, ecce cognovi, per receptionem pietatis tuæ et gratiæ, seu effectum precis devotæ, quoniam Deus meus es, id est, quod specialiter sis Deus meus, providens mihi et diligens me. Hinc enim Christus affirmat: Amen dico vobis, si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Petite, et accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum.
paras.en: [[55:10|Then shall my enemies be turned back|Tunc convertentur inimici mei retrorsum]]: that is, when thou hast heard me making supplication, my enemies visible and invisible shall fail. Hence too blessed James: [[Jas 4:7|resist|Resistite]] (he says) [[Jas 4:7|the devil: and he will fly from you|diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. [[55:10|In what day soever I shall call upon thee|In quacumque die invocavero te]] with an inward, affectionate and steadfast calling, [[55:10|behold I know|ecce cognovi]], by receiving thy loving-kindness and grace, or by the effect of devout prayer, that [[55:10|thou art my God|quoniam Deus meus es]], that is, that thou art in a special way my God, providing for me and loving me. For hence Christ affirms: [[John 16:23|Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father any thing in my name, he will give it you|Amen dico vobis, si quid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis]]. [[John 16:24|Ask, and you shall receive; that your joy may be full|Petite, et accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum]].

paras.t: In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, id est promissiones seu affectus quibus obligavi me tibi serviturum, et quibus te honorare desidero.
